Samsung motion photos keep their video: the still is re-encoded to HEIC and the original video is re-attached, so it still plays. A motion photo whose video can\'t be carried across is skipped rather than flattened. \"Only keep if smaller\" still applies.
Move originals to the trash instead of deleting
They can be restored from the gallery\'s trash for 30 days. The space only comes back when the trash empties.
Keep the screen on while converting
With the screen off the phone runs the app on its slow cores: a song that takes a minute takes ten or more.
A run pauses when the charger is unplugged and carries on when it is back. Runs always pause while the phone is too hot.

One folder per line, as it appears under the phone\'s storage, e.g. DCIM/Wallpaper/. Everything inside is left out of every run and the clean-up. Android/ covers the pictures other apps keep for themselves (WhatsApp, for one): a converted copy cannot go back there, and deleting the original breaks that app\'s own records.
Every run writes a log: its settings, each file that failed and why, and a closing summary. The 30 newest are kept under Android/data/com.example.convertjpgtoheic/files/logs.
No run has been logged yet.
Dry run: measure only, change nothing
Pictures, videos and music are converted to measure the real saving, then thrown away. Nothing is added and nothing deleted. Takes as long as a real run. Off again each time the app opens.

Re-encodes the JPG and PNG pictures in this range as HEIC, usually about half the size, keeping dates, location and rotation. Uses the quality, options and delete setting above; each HEIC is checked before its original is offered for deletion.

Deletes originals that were converted but never removed, because a run was cancelled or its delete prompt declined: pictures (JPG, PNG) with a HEIC and videos with an _HEVC copy, both in this range, and songs (MP3, M4A, FLAC) of any date with an Opus copy. Each video\'s copy then takes the original\'s name.

resources.string: Re-encodes videos (MP4, MOV) in this range from H.264 to HEVC, usually about half the size. Slow motion, hyperlapse and other special camera modes are left alone. Uses the delete and \"only keep if smaller\" options above.

Each H.264 video in this range is re-encoded as HEVC on the phone's own encoder. The capture date, location and orientation are copied across and the result is checked against the original before it is kept.

While both exist, the new copy is called name_HEVC.mp4. Once you confirm deleting the original it takes the original's name.

Videos take far longer than photos, and the phone gets warm: best done while charging.

resources.string: Re-encodes every MP3, M4A and FLAC in your music library as Opus (.opus), keeping title, artist, album and cover. A song is only kept as .opus if it comes out smaller. Covers the whole library, not just this range. Uses the delete option above.

Each MP3, M4A and FLAC in your music library is re-encoded as Opus and saved beside it as name.opus, with its tags and cover copied across. A copy is only kept if it is smaller than the original, and only after it has been checked against it.

You will be asked to confirm deleting the originals every 100 songs. Playlists that list the originals will lose those songs; the new copies can be added back.

Re-encoding a compressed file loses a little quality. It is rarely audible at the bitrates used, but the originals cannot be got back once deleted.

Each MP3, M4A and FLAC in your music library is re-encoded as Opus and saved beside it as name.opus, with its tags and cover copied across. A copy is only kept if it is smaller than the original, and only after it has been checked against it.\n\n\"Delete originals\" is off, so the originals will be kept and both copies will show in your music app.

resources.string: Fixes HEICs that show sideways in some viewers (Phone Link, for one) or that have lost their date and sit at the top of the gallery. Checks your whole library, not just this range. Only the photo\'s details are rewritten — never the picture.

This checks every HEIC on the phone and fixes two things:

• Rotation — so photos stand the right way up in every viewer, not just some.
• Capture date — so photos that lost theirs go back where they belong in the gallery. Where the original timezone is unknown, New Zealand time is assumed.

The picture itself is never touched. Android will ask you to allow the changes for photos this app no longer owns.

This finds every .m4p song on the phone. They are iTunes Store purchases whose audio is encrypted, so no Android app can play them, and they cannot be converted.\n\nAndroid will show you the songs and ask you to confirm before anything is deleted.
